email.subject: For the festive table, and every day after
email.preheader: Three pieces for sweets, light and the evening pour.
email.body:
The festive table fills slowly: sweets first, then the lamps, then the people. {p1} sits at the centre, a glass lid over steel compartments, ready for cardamom and cloves.

Set {p2} where the light falls, deep at the centre and open at the rim. Beside it goes the moonlit brass lamp from the same line, small enough for the corner where you light a diya.

{p3} is for the evening after, when the house is quiet and the tea gets poured.

email.subject: For the festive table, and every day after
email.preheader: Three pieces for sweets, light and the evening pour.
email.body:
The festive table fills slowly. Sweets come first, then the lamps, then the people, and at last the long talk that runs past midnight. {p1} sits at the centre of it all, a glass lid over steel compartments, ready for cardamom, cloves and the foil that nobody eats but everybody keeps.

Set {p2} at the edge, where the light falls, deep at the centre and open at the rim, so the fruit stays in view and the children can reach it.

{p3} waits for the evening after, when the house is quiet again, the guests are home, the plates are washed—and the tea gets poured, unhurried, for whoever is still awake—and still talking.
